explanation: Each term is 4 more than the one before, so the next is 19 + 4 = 23. A constant difference is the first thing to test on any number series.
Each term is three times the one before: 54 x 3 = 162. When the differences grow quickly, test a constant RATIO before anything more elaborate.
These are the squares 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, so the next is 6 squared = 36. The distractor 49 skips a step to 7 squared.
They are the prime numbers in order, so after 13 comes 17. 15 is 3 x 5 and 16 is even, so neither is prime; 19 skips 17.
Each term is the sum of the two before it: 8 + 13 = 21. Doubling the last term gives 26, which fits the recent growth but not the rule.
Each term is double the previous plus one: 79 x 2 + 1 = 159. Doubling alone gives 158, which is the near miss this series is built to catch.
Each term is double the previous plus one: 47 x 2 + 1 = 95. Checking the differences first (3, 6, 12, 24) also works — they double, so the next difference is 48.
The differences are 21, 19, 17, 15 — falling by two — so the next is 13 and the term is 48 - 13 = 35. (The terms are also n squared minus 1 for n = 11 down to 6, and 6 squared - 1 = 35.)

Two interleaved series: 7, 8, 9 in the odd positions and 10, 11, 12 in the even ones. The next belongs to the first, so it is 10. Looking for one rule across all six terms is what makes this look harder than it is.
These are the cubes 1, 8, 27, 64, so the next is 5 cubed = 125. The distractors are 10 squared, 11 squared and 9 squared, which is what reaching for squares gives.
The multipliers rise by one each step: x2, x3, x4, so next is x5 and 72 x 5 = 360. Keeping the last multiplier gives 288, which is the trap in every series of this shape.
The rest are cubes: 2, 3, 4 and 5 cubed. 100 is a square, not a cube. 64 is both 4 cubed and 8 squared, which is why it is the tempting wrong answer.

text: What comes next? C, F, I, L, ...
explanation: The letters advance by three: C(3), F(6), I(9), L(12), so the next is the 15th letter, O. Counting two forward gives N.

text: What comes next? AZ, BY, CX, DW, ...
explanation: The first letter moves forward (A, B, C, D, E) while the second moves back from Z (Z, Y, X, W, V). So EV. Each half has its own direction, which is the one thing to check in a paired-letter series.

text: What comes next? B2, D4, F6, H8, ...
explanation: The letters skip one each time (B, D, F, H, J) and the numbers rise by two (2, 4, 6, 8, 10), so J10. I is the next letter in plain order, which is why it appears twice among the distractors.

text: What comes next? Z, W, S, N, ...
explanation: Counting back through the alphabet the gaps grow: Z to W is 3, W to S is 4, S to N is 5, so the next gap is 6. Six before N (14) is the 8th letter, H.
